source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Avoid padding because pressure redistribution devices can interfere with the sterile surgical field","B":"Pad vulnerable bony prominences, maintain alignment, and reassess positioning throughout the case","C":"Delay all positioning reassessment until the procedure ends unless the client can report discomfort","D":"Use extra-tight safety straps over bony areas so the client cannot shift during the procedure"}}
source_row.rationale: Perioperative pressure-injury prevention includes proper positioning, pressure redistribution/padding for vulnerable areas, and ongoing reassessment. Immobility during surgery increases pressure-injury risk.
source_row.source_detail: 2026 positioning safety guidance: padding bony prominences, alignment, and continued reassessment; accessed 2026-08-14.
source_row.source_name: AORN — Positioning and Perioperative Pressure Injury Guidance
source_row.stem: A client is positioned for a prolonged operative procedure. Which nursing action most directly reduces positioning-related pressure injury risk?
